record.original_question: Fix an interval I contained in R and a subset B contained in R. Can one construct a family of measures {mu_beta} such that for every subset J of I the singular part of mu_beta gives J positive mass exactly for parameters beta in B, while the absolutely continuous part of mu_beta gives J positive mass for every beta in R?

evidence.quote: In fact, it possible to produce most any type of singular spectrum in this setting, see [13].

Open question (see [13]): Fix an interval I ⊂ R and subset B ⊂ R. Can one find a family of measures µβ so that (µβ)s(J) > 0 if and only if β ∈ B and (µβ)ac(J) > 0 for all β ∈ R and for every subset J ⊂ I?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a fixed interval and let $B \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a fixed subset. For each $\beta \in \mathbb{R}$, let $\mu_\beta$ be a Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}$, and write $\mu_\beta = (\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{ac}} + (\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{s}}$ for its Lebesgue decomposition into an absolutely continuous part and a singular part (with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$).

Determine whether one can construct a family of Borel measures $\{\mu_\beta\}_{\beta \in \mathbb{R}}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that for every Borel subset $J \subset I$ the following two conditions hold simultaneously:

(i) $(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{s}}(J) > 0$ if and only if $\beta \in B$;

(ii) $(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{ac}}(J) > 0$ for every $\beta \in \mathbb{R}$.

That is, can the parameter set governing positive singular mass on every sub-interval be prescribed to be exactly $B$, while the absolutely continuous part assigns positive mass to every such subset for all parameters $\beta$?
artifact.category_tag: Spectral measures and mixed spectral types
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related work on families of spectral measures with mixed types (e.g., constructions via Pick/Herglotz function representations) and on prescribing singular spectrum, but no source was located that explicitly resolves the prescribed-parameter-set question for the singular part while requiring full absolutely continuous support across all parameters. The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Families of Spectral Measures with Mixed Types
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of families where all operators have dense absolutely continuous and dense singular spectrum, via integral representations of Pick functions.
status_evidence.claim: Related constructions exist but do not directly settle the prescribed-B question.

status_evidence.title: Mixed spectral types for the one frequency discrete quasi-periodic Schrödinger operator
status_evidence.snippet: Coexistence of absolutely continuous and point/singular continuous spectrum for various parameters in quasi-periodic operators.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates mixed-type phenomena in parameter families, related but distinct from the precise prescription question.
